Write a generator that counts up to N, and explain why it saves memory.

Supplied answer
def count_up_to(n):
    count = 1
    while count <= n: # condition must use n
        yield count
        count += 1
for num in count_up_to(5):
    print(num, end=" ")
# a generator makes values one by one, so 10 lakh numbers
# do not have to sit in memory together
Note: Generators are lazy: they produce one value at a time instead of building a full list.
